key_insight: PRO-LONG shows that keeping a complete structured interaction log and searching it programmatically can substantially improve long-horizon LLM agent performance without bloating context.
engineering_relevance: For agent builders, the paper suggests a practical memory-management design that can raise accuracy while reducing token use, making long-horizon systems more efficient and scalable.
method: Store every interaction in a complete structured history instead of pruning aggressively.
Use coding-agent-style search over the log to retrieve only relevant details into context.
Optimize context management as a memory-plus-retrieval problem for exploratory tasks.
evidence_signal: On the full ARC-AGI-3 public game set, PRO-LONG improved a base coding agent by 18.0 percentage points on average across frontier models and reached up to 76.1% pass@1 with 4.2–5.8x fewer tokens.
watch_item: Performance depends on effective history search and log structure, so weaker retrieval or poorly organized traces could reduce the gains in more complex deployments.
paper_title: PRO-LONG: Programmatic Memory Enables Long-Horizon Reasoning
